stem:
Rudo Chikore owns a hardware shop in Kwekwe. Her trial balance at 30 June 2025 did not agree and the difference was entered in a suspense account. Her draft income statement showed a net profit of US\$13,742. The following errors were then found:

| No. | Error |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | The sales journal was undercast by US\$1,100. |
| 2 | Repairs to the delivery van, US\$386, were debited to the motor vehicles account. |
| 3 | Discount received of US\$157 in the cash book was not posted to the discount received account. |
| 4 | Wages of US\$1,245 paid by bank were posted to the wages account as US\$1,425. |
| 5 | A cheque for US\$694 received from Mlambo, a debtor, was credited to his account as US\$649. |
| 6 | Goods of US\$238 returned to Zhou, a creditor, were correctly debited to Zhou's account and also debited to the returns outwards account. |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which error did **not** affect the agreement of the trial balance?

options.rationale: Correct: an error of principle with equal debit and credit.
Wages were debited 180 too much: the totals disagreed.
Mlambo was credited 45 too little: the totals disagreed.
Two debits and no credit: the totals disagreed.

parts.explanation: Error 2 put the right amount on each side, in the wrong class of account.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the difference in books that was entered in the suspense account. (It was entered on the credit side.)
parts.explanation: Suspense entries needed: debit 1,100 (sales) + 157 (discount received) + 180 (wages) + 45 (Mlambo) + 476 (returns outwards, twice 238) = 1,958. No suspense entries are credits, so the account was opened with a credit of 1,958: the debit side of the trial balance was larger. Using 238 instead of 476 for error 6 gives 1,720.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Suspense entries needed: debit 1,100 (sales) + 157 (discount received) + 180 (wages) + 45 (Mlambo) + 476 (returns outwards, twice 238) = 1,958. No suspense entries are credits, so the account was opened with a credit of 1,958: the debit side of the trial balance was larger. Using 238 instead of 476 for error 6 gives 1,720.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Prepare journal entries to correct errors 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6. Narratives are not required.

points.description: Error 2: debit motor repairs 386; credit motor vehicles 386
Error 3: debit suspense 157; credit discount received 157
Error 6: debit suspense 476; credit returns outwards 476

parts.explanation: One side to the wrong account, the other to suspense (except error 2).

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Complete the journal entry to correct error 5, and the amount of the correction for error 6.

payload.template: Error 5: debit {{blank:a}} US\$45; credit {{blank:b}} US\$45. Error 6: returns outwards is credited with US\$ {{blank:c}}.

parts.explanation: Mlambo was credited 649 instead of 694: credit Mlambo 45 more; the other side is suspense. Returns outwards was debited 238 instead of credited, so it needs a credit of $2 \times 238 = 476$.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Prepare the suspense account, showing the difference in books.

points.description: Difference in books 1,958 on the credit side
Sales 1,100, Discount received 157, Wages 180, Mlambo 45 and Returns outwards 476 on the debit side
Totals 1,958 on each side; no balance remains

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Calculate Rudo's corrected net profit for the year ended 30 June 2025.
parts.explanation: 13,742 + 1,100 (sales) + 157 (discount received) + 180 (wages) + 476 (returns outwards) − 386 (motor repairs) = 15,269. Error 5 has no effect on profit.
parts.workedSolution: 1. 13,742 + 1,100 (sales) + 157 (discount received) + 180 (wages) + 476 (returns outwards) − 386 (motor repairs) = 15,269. Error 5 has no effect on profit.

explanation: This item tests the suspense account, journal corrections and the corrected net profit (ZIMSEC Paper 2 style).
hints: For each error write: done, should have been, correction.
Suspense takes the other side whenever only one side was wrong.

stem:
Sipho Dube runs a printing business in Bulawayo. On 30 November 2025 his cash book showed a debit bank balance of US\$3,184. When he received his bank statement for November he found:

| No. | Item |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Bank charges of US\$57 had not been entered in the cash book |
| 2 | A standing order for rent of US\$725 had not been entered in the cash book |
| 3 | Lobengula School, a debtor, had paid US\$1,860 directly into the bank by credit transfer |
| 4 | A cheque for US\$412 from N. Sibanda, a debtor, had been dishonoured |
| 5 | A direct debit of US\$136 for insurance had not been entered in the cash book |
| 6 | A cheque for US\$529 paid to Ncube Paper had been entered in the cash book as US\$592 |
| 7 | Interest of US\$19 had been added to the account by the bank |
| 8 | Cheques to Mzilikazi Inks (US\$1,147) and Tshabalala Motors (US\$388) had not been presented for payment |
| 9 | Takings of US\$2,265 deposited on 30 November did not appear on the statement |
| 10 | The bank had credited Sipho's account with a deposit of US\$240 belonging to another customer |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which items are **not** entered in the updated cash book?

options.rationale: Charges, standing orders and direct debits must be entered.
These were unknown to Sipho and must be entered.
Correct: timing differences and a bank error belong in the reconciliation.
Item 6 is Sipho's own error and must be corrected in the cash book.

parts.explanation: Only items the business did not know about and its own errors are entered in the cash book.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the updated cash book balance at 30 November 2025.
parts.explanation: Item 6: the payment was overstated by 592 − 529 = 63, so 63 is debited. Debits: 3,184 + 1,860 + 63 + 19 = 5,126. Credits: 57 + 725 + 412 + 136 = 1,330. Balance = 5,126 − 1,330 = 3,796 debit.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Item 6: the payment was overstated by 592 − 529 = 63, so 63 is debited. Debits: 3,184 + 1,860 + 63 + 19 = 5,126. Credits: 57 + 725 + 412 + 136 = 1,330. Balance = 5,126 − 1,330 = 3,796 debit.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Prepare Sipho's updated cash book (bank columns) and bring down the balance on 1 December 2025.

points.description: Balance b/d 3,184, credit transfer 1,860, error 63 and interest 19 on the debit side
Bank charges 57, rent 725, dishonoured cheque 412 and insurance 136 on the credit side
Balance c/d 3,796 dated 30 Nov; totals 5,126 on both sides
Balance b/d 3,796 on the debit side dated 1 Dec

answerSpec.modelAnswer:

parts.explanation: Items 8 to 10 are left for the reconciliation.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate the balance shown on the bank statement at 30 November 2025.
parts.explanation: 3,796 + 1,147 + 388 (unpresented cheques) − 2,265 (uncredited deposit) + 240 (bank error: the bank shows more than it should) = 3,306.
parts.workedSolution: 1. 3,796 + 1,147 + 388 (unpresented cheques) − 2,265 (uncredited deposit) + 240 (bank error: the bank shows more than it should) = 3,306.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Prepare Sipho's bank reconciliation statement at 30 November 2025, starting with the updated cash book balance.

points.description: Add bank error 240; less uncredited deposit 2,265

|  |  | 1,775 |
| **Less:** Uncredited deposit |  | (2,265) |
| **Balance as per bank statement** |  | **3,306** |

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: State **two** reasons why Sipho should prepare a bank reconciliation statement every month.

points.description: One reason: to check the cash book balance is correct / detect errors by the business or the bank
Second reason: to detect fraud / identify old unpresented cheques / keep records up to date

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: To check that his cash book balance is correct and find errors (such as the bank's 240 error), and to detect fraud or cheques that have been unpresented for a long time.

explanation: This item tests the updated cash book and the bank reconciliation statement (ZIMSEC Paper 2 style).
hints: Update the cash book first; leave timing differences and bank errors for the reconciliation.
